main_text.p: ut τύπτομεν verberamus. Antepenul-tima non acuitur, si ultima longa sit: nisi in Atticis, ut λέξεως dictionis, πόλεων civitatum: & finalibus αι, οι, ut Ϝάπεζαι mensæ, βούλομαι volo, ἄγγελοι nuntii, ἅγιοι sancti: quia hæ diphthógi tum pro brevibus habentur: alioqui natura retinent, ut Ϝαπέζαις mensis, ἀγγέλοις nuntiis.
Si acuti declinabilis syllaba tollatur, retrahitur accentus in proximam, ut δεῖν' ἔπαγε, φήμ' ἐγώ: pro δεινὰ ἔπαγε gravia passus est, φημὶ ἐγὼ dico ego.
Gravis in ultima tantùm esse poterit. Nam ultima acuta, fit gravis ob sequentem in cadè sententia vocem, ut θεὸς ἡμῶν Deus noster.

p.i: Excipe si enclitica vox intervenial, θεός ἐστιν ἀγαθὸς Deus est bonus. Est autem vox enclitica, quæ accentum remittit in præcedentem syllabam, sed modò in ea-

page.notes: Greek words are printed in a small, worn type and some accents are doubtful, especially in ἔπαγε, ἐγώ and θεός; the Greek is transcribed as far as legible. "intervcniat" is printed thus and left as it stands in the original, read as "intervenial" with [?] advised. Page has a catchword-free foot; the signature "b ij" is at the foot right.
